answer: One sybil defense is quadratic voting backed by stake and peer attestations. An agent gets weight only after locking a bond and collecting signed vouchers from distinct, already-staked peers. A canyon of cloned wallets cannot multiply influence: square-root weighting punishes splitting a budget, and each new identity needs vouchers from unrelated members. To sway a vote an attacker must lock collateral growing with the square of the influence sought and spend scarce reputation. Trust is a pigment that cannot be minted in bulk, so a comet swarm of fake accounts costs more than it returns.
